minutes.headline: Selectmen approved end-of-year FY13 budget transfers, contingent on Finance Committee, and agreed to add the fence to the Tri-Town license.
minutes.summary: The board heard the town manager's FY13 closeout and local receipts review, and voted on Chapter 44 Section 33B transfers to cover overdrawn lines, contingent on Finance Committee approval. Committee reports were long, dominated by a debate over the fence at the Tri-Town development, and the board reached a majority view to amend the license to include the fence. Two reappointments were voted and the board moved to a non-televised workshop on policies.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public discussion; none came from the public.

Reappoint Stanley Young as constable and Gene Larkin to the senior tax work-off committee

budget_items.what_was_said: Transfers between appropriation groupings after year end are limited to the greater of three percent or a fixed dollar amount.
Town manager listed amounts returned by grouping and an overage in general government to encumber money for bylaw codification; net return on a roughly 30 million budget.

budget_items.what_was_said: Transfers to legal expense from unemployment, veterans, and registrar of graves for bylaw codification, plus a transfer to weights and measures for one-time equipment.
A member questioned whether the eleven thousand transfer exceeded the cap; manager said the test applies to the whole unclassified appropriation.
Local receipts came in slightly under budget with variances in motor vehicle excise, penalties and interest, Tri-Town school rental, ambulance, permits, and supplemental tax.
A water betterment payment is behind and expected to catch up.
Low bid for asphalt was less per ton than before, on a one-year contract with extension options.
Outsourced pump maintenance bid is below current estimated spending.
Town manager said the road plan is underfunded and roads are deteriorating faster than progress.

what_happened.line: The board voted on end-of-year budget transfers under Chapter 44 Section 33B, contingent on Finance Committee approval; the recording does not make the outcome audible.
A majority of the board agreed to amend the Tri-Town license to include the fence, after a long committee-report debate.
The Townsend IMA and both PILOT agreements were continued, the PILOTs pending the developers' response.
The board reappointed a constable and a member of the senior tax work-off committee, and the vote passed.
The town manager said the road plan is underfunded and roads are deteriorating faster than progress, and the DPW director is set to present on August 13.

why_it_matters: The transfers move money between lines to cover overdrawn accounts, including legal costs for bylaw codification, and take effect only if the Finance Committee approves them.
An underfunded road plan means road repair may compete for money in a future budget or at Town Meeting, and the PILOT agreements affect what the new developments pay toward town services.
watch_next: August 13: the DPW director presents the road maintenance and street sign database.
Next week or the first week of August: the Townsend IMA returns, and the PILOT agreements return once the developers respond.
